collection_summary: This instance is a curated, source-defined ground truth listing the 66 countries and dependencies whose Wikipedia-cited renewable share of electricity production was strictly more than 50% at the snapshot date, with the share, the dominant renewable source (Hydro, Wind, Solar, Biofuels, or Other), and the year of the reported statistic (2022–2025 depending on entity). The row set is what the cited Wikipedia article's percentage-share wikitable reports under its 'countries and dependencies' framing for entities with renewable share strictly greater than 50%; aggregate region rows (World, EU, OECD, continents, etc.) are excluded by the construction rule, and exact-50% rows (Cook Islands and Greece) are excluded by the strict 'more than 50%' filter.
source_coverage_notes:
Roles:
- source_urls[0] (List_of_countries_by_electricity_production_from_renewable_sources): universe + filter + value (defines the country universe; supplies Renewable Share, the Hydro/Wind/Solar/Biofuels/Other sub-components from which the Dominant Renewable Source is derived, and the per-country reporting Year)

Single-source Tier B instance. The article cites Ember/IEA as its underlying data provider; this benchmark instance treats the Wikipedia article as the canonical staged source and Ember/IEA as upstream data. No separate validation source. Year heterogeneity (2022-2025) is intrinsic to the article's per-country reporting cadence; the staged Year cell is verbatim from the article's Year column.
decision_log:
Candidate card (per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: Pass. Universe (countries and dependencies with Wikipedia-cited renewable share strictly greater than 50%) is fully source-defined via the article's filter cell; Wikipedia's article is the authoritative aggregator of Ember/IEA per-country data. Table is LLM-knowable for a pre-2025 cutoff: top entities (Iceland 100%, Bhutan 100%, Norway 99%, Paraguay 100%, Costa Rica 94%) are widely-known facts; the tail (Sierra Leone 95%, Honduras 62%, Greenland 87%, Central African Republic 100%) tests less-confident knowledge. Row count (66) is comfortably in protocol range. Confidence gradient is real (Iceland/Norway/Costa Rica very memorable; African and dependency tail less so).
- Seed/provenance: original instance, not derived from a seed in example_questions.txt. Picker recommended an original Environment / Education instance to plant one of the two remaining family-level gaps (after Law was planted on 2026-04-30 by landmark_us_supreme_court_decisions_by_chief_justice).
- Category: set_filter (gap 2) primary; comparative (gap 4) plausible secondary because the >50% threshold implicitly compares each country against the threshold. Primary set_filter pairs canonically with operation_type=filter per references/artifact-contract.md.
- Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, single source URL; gt_construction = manual_wikipedia; source_count = 1.
- Expected shape: 66 rows x 4 columns; PK = Country.
- Domain: Environment/Energy — the **first instance in the Environment family**, leaving only Education unrepresented at the family level.
- Risks/adaptation: The >50% threshold sits near the band where countries drift in and out year-to-year (Netherlands 51%, UK 52% are the closest current rows; Greece 50% and Cook Islands 50% are dropped by the strict filter). Year heterogeneity (2022-2025) is documented per-row.
- Decision: Stage.

Why original rather than seed-driven: no seed in example_questions.txt targets renewables, climate, or environment broadly; an original Environment-family instance was the highest-priority pick per the 2026-04-30 picker snapshot's selection rubric (★★★★ for an original Environment / Education instance because two family-level gaps remained).

Year-anchor decision: the user initially proposed a strict 2023 anchor for source-defined-claim consistency with prior instances (the 'as of [year]' anchor pattern from nobel_categories_2020_2024_laureates and top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent). After probing the source, a strict 2023 filter would yield 28 rows (still above the row-count gate) but would exclude the canonically-known renewable leaders Norway, Costa Rica, Denmark, Sweden, New Zealand, Brazil, Switzerland, Spain, UK, Canada, and Germany — all of which the source reports under 2024 or 2025 vintages. This would weaken the calibration test by filtering out most of the LLM-easy rows. After discussion, the per-country most-recent-year approach was chosen instead, which (a) keeps all 66 high-renewable entities (after the strict-50 filter applied during the post-audit repair), (b) matches the per-row Year precedent set by top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent (whose Year column was 2021-2025 depending on the per-continent source), and (c) keeps the source-defined claim honest — each cell is the value the Wikipedia table reports for that country at the snapshot date.

Category <-> operation_type pairing: query_category=set_filter pairs canonically with operation_type=filter per references/artifact-contract.md. The single-WHERE-predicate shape (renewable_share_pct > 50) is the canonical set_filter primitive.

Domain selection: Environment/Energy is a new family in the benchmark (previously Law / Environment / Education were unrepresented at the family level; Law was planted on 2026-04-30, this instance plants Environment, leaving only Education).

Post-audit (2026-05-01): two BLOCKING fixes and two NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE fixes applied. (a) BLOCKING #1: title-vs-filter mismatch — the title says 'more than 50%' but the staged CSV used '>= 50%' which incorrectly included exact-50% rows (Cook Islands at 50% Solar 2022, Greece at 50% Solar 2025). Resolved by tightening the filter to strict > 50% and dropping Cook Islands and Greece; row count 68 → 66. The natural 'more than 50%' title and the 'over_50pct' instance id are preserved by this choice (the alternative — change wording to 'at least 50%' — was rejected because it would require renaming the instance id and four staged files for a less-natural-language phrasing). (b) BLOCKING #2: scope-claim mismatch — the cited Wikipedia article is explicitly framed as 'countries and dependencies' rather than 'sovereign countries only', and the staged set includes Greenland (autonomous territory of Denmark), French Guiana (overseas region of France), and previously Cook Islands (free-association state with NZ; dropped by the strict-50 filter). Resolved by changing the collection_summary, decision_log, and _extraction_notes language from 'sovereign countries' to 'countries and dependencies' to match the source's framing. (c) NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE #3: _extraction_notes said '12 countries reach 100% in the snapshot' but the actual staged count is 9 (Albania, Bhutan, Central African Republic, DR Congo, Ethiopia, Iceland, Lesotho, Nepal, Paraguay); corrected to '9 entities reach 100%'. (d) NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE #4: _extraction_notes said the lone Other-dominant country was Iceland (geothermal); the actual staged Other-dominant country is Kenya (43% Other / geothermal, with Hydro at 28%). Iceland's 30% Other is dominated by its 70% Hydro and so its row's Dominant Renewable Source is Hydro, not Other. Corrected to 'Other 1 (Kenya — 43% geothermal); Iceland's 30% Other (also geothermal) is dominated by its 70% Hydro and is therefore Hydro-dominant rather than Other-dominant'.
normalization_decisions: Universe definition: the staged universe is countries and dependencies with Wikipedia-cited renewable share strictly greater than 50% in the percentage-share wikitable of the cited article. The article's framing is 'countries and dependencies' rather than 'sovereign countries only', so dependent territories (Greenland — autonomous Danish territory; French Guiana — overseas French region) are kept as the source presents them. Aggregate region rows (World, European Union, OECD, North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, Americas, Oceania, Non-OECD, Latin America, Middle East, Sub-Saharan Africa) are excluded; they are listed in the same wikitable but are not country-or-dependency rows. Exact-50% rows (Cook Islands at 50% Solar 2022, Greece at 50% Solar 2025) are excluded by the strict 'more than 50%' filter. Renewable Share normalization: the 'Renew.' column value is taken verbatim as a numeric percentage with one decimal place; values are >50.0-100.0 across the staged set. Dominant Renewable Source: derived from the row's per-source columns (Hydro %, Wind %, Solar %, Biofuels %, Other %) by selecting the source with the highest percentage. Source labels are normalized: the Wikipedia column header 'Bio.' becomes 'Biofuels' for the staged Dominant Renewable Source cell value (matches the article's prose usage); the 'Other' column is preserved as 'Other'. The lone Other-dominant row in the staged set is Kenya (43% Other / geothermal, with Hydro at 28%). Iceland's 30% Other (also geothermal) is dominated by its 70% Hydro, so Iceland's Dominant Renewable Source is Hydro, not Other. No tie-breaking was needed in the snapshot — every country in the staged set has a unique max sub-source. Year normalization: the per-country 'Year' cell is taken verbatim as a 4-digit integer; the snapshot's Year distribution is 2022 (7 entities), 2023 (28), 2024 (14), 2025 (17). Country names follow the cited Wikipedia article's English forms verbatim, including 'DR Congo' (the article's short form for Democratic Republic of the Congo), 'Eswatini' (post-2018 official form, not 'Swaziland'), 'North Korea' (not 'Democratic People's Republic of Korea'), and 'Cook Islands' (which the article includes despite being a self-governing state in free association with New Zealand rather than a fully sovereign UN member).
open_questions: 1. Whether to add a Continent column for richer geographic partitioning. The cited Wikipedia article does not include a Continent column; adding it would require either Wikidata SPARQL (P30) as a second source (introducing the multi-continent-Wikidata-tagging quirks documented in top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent's curation) or a hand-mapped continent column that adds curator judgment. Current design omits Continent to keep source_count = 1 and stay strictly source-defined. 2. Whether to anchor the Year column to a single year and accept the lossy filter (strict 2023 = 28 rows; misses Norway/Costa Rica/Denmark/Sweden/NZ). The user-decided answer is no; the per-country Year column reflects the source's heterogeneous reporting cadence and matches the top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent precedent. 3. Whether dependencies should be excluded from the universe to keep the table to fully UN-recognized sovereign states only. The current design follows the source's 'countries and dependencies' framing verbatim and includes Greenland and French Guiana as dependent rows; a v2 could narrow to sovereign states and exclude these two rows. (Cook Islands was the third dependency in the original probe set but is excluded by the strict >50% filter.) 4. Whether 'Renewable share' should be split into 'low-carbon share' (renewable + nuclear), which is sometimes the more decision-relevant policy metric. The cited article reports renewables only; a v2 could add a nuclear-share column or switch to the low-carbon framing for a different question.
